Folks — adding technical provenance detail to include in the packet for Bedrock:

- Deletion mechanism: ephemeral logs are stored in a segmented S3 bucket namespace (tenant-scoped prefix). A scheduled lifecycle worker runs per-region and enqueues deletion tasks to a durable job queue. Each deletion task writes a deletion manifest record to our immutable manifest store (append-only) with fields: manifest_id, object_id(s) (hashed), deletion_timestamp_utc, worker_id, job_id, pre_delete_hash, post_delete_hash, retention_hold_id (nullable).

- Cryptographic checks: pre_delete_hash is the SHA256 of the object at rest (stored separately and rotated). post_delete_hash is an HMAC over the manifest fields, signed by our key in KMS. We include the manifest_id and HMAC value in the evidence packet so Bedrock can verify the manifest integrity.

- Exception handling: When a legal/forensic hold is requested the retention_hold_id is created, associated job tasks are moved to a hold queue, and the manifest store records hold_start_ts and expected_release_ts. Approval is role-based (Legal Lead + CS Director). We will include a redacted approval trail and the policy excerpt.

- Retention windows: default ephemeral TTL = 30 days; customers on HIPAA plan can request 90 days; any customer-specific deviations are documented in tenant metadata and require a formal change order.

I suggest we:
1) Include one canonical manifest (redacted) and the associated audit log slice.
2) Provide the HMAC verification steps (how Bedrock can validate HMAC using the metadata we provide).
3) Add a short CAIQ/SIG table mapping (Markus to finalize).
